[quote=greater_rostoria;60891597][b]Antonio Consortium Acquires Shahrestan Olympic Stadium:[/b]

The Antonio Consortium has been scooping up and taking large chunks of the Valderran economy ever since the newly established government gave permission for them and three other UREV corporations to take charge in the development and stability of the country. Large domestic businesses have been purchased and turned into subsidiaries under the Antonio Consortium, while large infrastructure projects and manufacturing hubs are sprung up from the pockets of the company.

And now the most recent acquisition on March 22nd of 2027 has seen the company purchase and gain full ownership of the Shahrestan Stadium as well as the broadcasting rights to the stadium and games played by the local football team. The Antonio Consortium invested millions into the local area, mainly in infrastructure and creatings jobs for the local population, and by purchasing this stadium it hopes to further expand their influence in the Valdderan market.

An Antonio Consortium spokesperson has stated that, [i]"millions more will be spent renovating and turning this stadium into a world-class location for fans of football."[/i] The company has begun renovations to expand capacity to 100,000 people and is modernising the interior and pitch, having partnered with Amery Holdings to receive construction support for the additional seating. The stadium and broadcast rights are reserved solely for the company, and with the upcoming football world cup, the first year revenue is expected to return millions in profits.

Alongside the stadium, Antonio Consortium will be purchasing local and foreign football talent and creating a new club, with an initial $200 million delegated to purchasing the best players they can. The football club created are the Shahrestan Lions, and their expected manager is to be Rurik Malddov, an experienced and long-time UREV manager who has won 4 Federal Cups. Antonio Consortium has managed to acquire free broadcasting rights when the Shahrestan Lions are playing, giving them no competitors for advertisement space.

[quote=vespurias;60875622]Sarsen was given an encouraging, or withering, glare from the other two as he was gestured to stand diplomatically next to the King for the first pictures and the handshake with a bright smile. Before they were taken the other two sipped the tea, although Sir Melville took short sips only, before they took the right positions for the second pictures, with the Secretary with his hands on his front, and  the representative held the trim of his suit.

Sir Walter would then go on to follow the King, and sign the document, when the representative passed him down a small golden cylinder, which Sir Walter unscrewed to show a red stamp, with the seal of the Prince, which he stamped right next to his signature. After that he'd offer to shake the King's Hand one last time as Sir Melville took the golden cylinder and screwed it back shut.

"It's been an honour, your royal Highness. We hope for a long and harmonious link between our nations." Walter said.[/quote]
As the King turned around, he placed the Great Seal of the Kingdom on top of his signature and shook Sir Walter Sarsen's hand. "Gentlemen, it's been a pleasure. I now have the joy of welcoming you to the Non-Aligned Bloc. We may rest easy knowing that peace is back on the table."

He walked with the Eneas' Diplomatic Envoy Group to their car waiting for them outside, wished them good travels, and returned to his office. He sat for a moment, looking at the document. He viewed it as an achievement and immediately ordered that it be put in the National Archives of Minhokae, in Government Complex Jincheon.

History was made on the 24th of March, 2027.
